scoring_justification: The checker recomputes the maximum stress, the stress at which split length first reaches 3.0 mm, and the peak stress ratio from the agent's raw CSV artifacts, comparing each to a hidden paper gold value with a tolerance. These are derived quantities, not directly submitted by the agent.

hidden_assets.purpose: hidden gold values for peak stress, split threshold stress, and ablation peak ratio
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper text: Section 6.2 reports baseline peak 433 MPa, Section 6.3 reports no-delamination peak 281 MPa and ratio ~1.54. Fig. 6 shows split length vs stress; at split length 3 mm the stress is approximately 330 MPa.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the paper's reported numbers and direct reading from the described figure.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the actual paper-reported quantities. The checker verifies that the agent's reproduced simulation reproduces these numbers to within reasonable tolerances.

schema.description: Rows in order of increasing displacement.

outputs.description: Far‑field stress vs. displacement from the full simulation; checker recomputes the maximum stress and compares it to the paper‑reported value within a tolerance.
Split length vs. applied stress; checker finds the stress at which split length first reaches a threshold and compares to the paper‑reported value within a tolerance.
Peak stresses from the two simulations; checker computes the ratio baseline_peak / no_delamination_peak and checks it lies within the paper‑reported range.

output_contract.notes: All scored CSVs contain raw simulation data that the checker recomputes to extract the relevant quantities (max stress, split-length threshold stress, peak ratio). The agent must implement the constitutive models and run the FE simulations; no pre‑computed artifacts are provided.

steps.description: Maximum stress from the load-displacement curve
Applied stress when split length first reaches 3.0 mm
Ratio of baseline peak stress to no-delamination peak stress
